about.tagline: Your Bambu Lab printer, one click away in the system tray.
about.how1: Bambu Bar connects straight to your printer on the local network, the same way Bambu Studio does in LAN mode: an encrypted MQTT connection on port 8883, signed in with the printer's access code. The printer's certificate is checked against the Bambu Lab certificate authorities bundled with the app — a connection from anything else is refused.
about.how2: The printer streams its status about once a second. Bambu Bar shows it in the system tray, watches the job it starts, and keeps a short history of your prints.
about.privacy: No account, no cloud, no analytics. Nothing leaves your network: Bambu Bar talks only to your printer. The access code is stored in the Windows Credential Manager — never in plain text — and only ever sent to the printer.
about.credits1: A Windows port of the independent macOS app Bambu Bar by rolottr (MIT). Protocol details and the English HMS error texts come from the open-source ha-bambulab project (MIT), with thanks to Bambuddy and bambu-cli for documenting the newer printers.
